sentences.text: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, an 8.4% net interest income CAGR and 6.2% noninterest income CAGR [D5][D206][F111][F112].
The path was a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue was $121.6 billion in FY2021 before jumping 22.9% in FY2023 and 12.3% in FY2024 [D110][D179][D202].
The FY2023 step came from higher rates lifting net interest income 33.8%, with deposit margin expansion on higher rates cited in the segment results [D174][P37].
FY2025 growth slowed to 2.8% as net interest income rose 3.1% and noninterest income 2.4%, with NII excluding Markets flat year over year [D226][D221][D222][P28].
North America supplied the bulk of growth, contributing 20.6pp of the FY2023 increase and 10.2pp in FY2024, but only 0.2pp in FY2025 [D245][D248][D251].
International is the faster-growing but smaller piece: Asia-Pacific grew 17.3% in FY2025 for 1.2pp of growth, and EMEA 9.5% for 1.2pp [D300][D301][D275][D276].
FY2025 NII growth came from higher Markets net interest income, higher Card Services revolving balances and higher wholesale deposits, offset by deposit margin compression [P28].
Profit grew faster than revenue over the window: net income CAGR of 9.7% exceeded the 6.2% noninterest income CAGR, and EPS CAGR of 13.9% exceeded net income growth [F113][F112][F115].
The gap is partly share count: diluted shares fell 3.4% in FY2025 and every year of the window, so EPS rose 1.4% while net income fell 2.6% [D224][D216][D214].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025, below its 57.2% window median and near the 51.7% window low set in FY2024 [D207][D333][D331].
That is well inside the banks peer median of 61.7%, placing JPM at the 0th percentile (best) of seven peers [D337][D336].

Noninterest expense rose 4.2% in FY2025, driven by higher compensation, brokerage and distribution fees, auto lease depreciation, technology and marketing, partly offset by FDIC special assessment releases [D225][P26].
Credit costs are the offsetting pressure: the provision was 7.8% of revenue in FY2025, up from 6.0% in FY2024 and above the 6.0% peer median [D208][D185][D341].
The FY2025 provision reflected net portfolio increases, credit quality changes on client-specific exposures, updated leveraged-loan loss assumptions and estimated borrower fraud losses [P15].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it was -$148 billion in FY2025 against $57.0 billion of net income [F60][F30].
The outflow came from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, net loan originations held-for-sale and higher other assets, partly offset by net income and higher trading liabilities [P21].
Capital return is the better lens: buybacks plus dividends of $48.2 billion in FY2025 were 85% of net income, up from $33.6 billion in FY2024 [D205][F30][D182].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025, against a banks peer median of 11.8% and at the 100th percentile of seven peers [D213][D339][D338].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits in FY2025, up from 55.0% in FY2024, as loans grew to $1.47 trillion and deposits to $2.56 trillion [D211][D188][X197][X207].
The loan growth was driven by higher CIB loans, primarily in Markets, and higher securities-based lending in AWM on client demand [P4].
Capital return rose to $48.2 billion in FY2025 from $33.6 billion, with buybacks of $31.6 billion and dividends of $16.6 billion, while diluted shares fell 3.4% [D205][D182][X102][X112][D224].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, and differs by up to 0.10% [R1][F26][X16][F30][X20].
The gap is small but matters at the margin: FY2025 10-K net income was $57.0 billion against $57.0 billion in the table, so growth rates shift slightly [X20][F30].
Credit quality is the substantive flag: criticized wholesale exposure rose to $48.5 billion from $44.7 billion, and nonaccrual exposure increased $273 million [P2][P1].
The increase was driven by downgrades and new commitments in SPEs, Consumer & Retail, Banks & Finance Companies, Healthcare and Chemicals & Plastics [P2].
Watch the efficiency ratio: a move back above the 57.2% window median would reverse the FY2024-FY2025 improvement, reported in the next 10-K [D333][D207].
Watch the provision: a rise above the 7.8% of revenue recorded in FY2025 would extend the credit-cost climb from 6.0% in FY2024 [D208][D185].
Watch net interest income: a return to the FY2021 level of $52.3 billion would signal the rate-driven step change has unwound, versus $95.4 billion in FY2025 [F6][F10].
